model.name: Live transport survives suspend/resume — reconnect + refetch-resync on visibility/pageshow, fail-loud, no UA-sniff (iOS lifecycle)
model.description: The live-MVC transport must SURVIVE suspend/resume. Live-MVC symptom is iOS-Safari-SPECIFIC (tester: a passive client updated from broadcast ALONE 3/3 on desktop-WebKit -> the general render path is RULED OUT). MECHANISM: iOS suspends WebSockets on background/lock -> the socket dies QUIETLY -> the DOM stays STALE -> only a manual reload resyncs = exactly Tron's symptom. FIX: ONE shared transport-lifecycle helper across BOTH transports; on visibilitychange->visible AND pageshow (bfcache restore): verify-or-reconnect + RE-SYNC by REFETCH (never trust in-memory after a suspend gap) + FAIL-LOUD if resync fails. NO UA-sniff — general-correct (fix the mechanism, works everywhere). Distinct LAYER from R37.12/R37.24 (view-bus/no-2nd-source, which ASSUME a live transport) and R40.45 (the sanctioned EMIT path); this is the TRANSPORT layer that keeps the bus alive to a resumed client. Grounds the liveness law one layer down: 'the user saw it move' requires the TRANSPORT survived, not just that data was correct + emitted.

discoverySource.measuredBy: robbin-tester (passive desktop-WebKit 3/3 -> general render path RULED OUT -> iOS-Safari-transport-specific)
discoverySource.rNumberRuledBy: robbin-req (structural: transport LAYER, distinct from R37.12/R37.24 view-bus + R40.45 emit-path; S37 realtime-MVC family)
discoverySource.mechanism: iOS suspends WS on bg/lock -> socket dies quietly -> DOM stale -> manual reload only resync

model.crossRefNote: The TRANSPORT layer under the realtime-MVC stack: R37.12 (ONE VIEW BUS) + R37.24 (bus-by-elimination) ASSUME a live transport — this keeps it alive across suspend/resume so their bus actually reaches a resumed iOS client. R40.45 (live-on-advance, sanctioned seam endpoint) is the EMIT-PATH this transport delivers; its liveness law (data-correct != user-saw-it-move) extends here one layer down: user-saw-it-move requires the TRANSPORT survived. NEW req not an extension: none of the three scope transport-lifecycle-resilience (reconnect/refetch-resync on visibility/pageshow, fail-loud, no UA-sniff).

acceptanceCriteria.text: ONE shared transport-lifecycle helper handles BOTH transports (no per-transport fork of reconnect/resync logic) — the DRY single-source that makes the behaviour identical across every live connection.

gateRef.assertion: reconnect/resync logic lives in ONE shared helper used by both transports; a per-transport fork => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING (scenario-first #126; expert fix pre-built 8d04af8a2 to design 0b9aa6dc7, marker pending): seed a 2nd transport with its own forked reconnect logic (not the shared helper) => RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: On visibilitychange->visible AND on pageshow (incl bfcache-restored persisted=true), the helper VERIFIES-OR-RECONNECTS the transport and RE-SYNCS the view. Both events are handled (pageshow catches the bfcache path visibilitychange misses).

gateRef.assertion: after a suspend gap, visibilitychange->visible AND pageshow(bfcache) each trigger verify-or-reconnect + resync

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING (scenario-first #126; expert fix pre-built 8d04af8a2 to design 0b9aa6dc7, marker pending): seed a bfcache restore (pageshow persisted) with a dead socket -> resync fires; not handling pageshow => stale

acceptanceCriteria.text: RESYNC refetches from the SOURCE (never trusts in-memory/DOM state after the gap) — a suspended client's in-memory model is presumed STALE until refetched.

gateRef.assertion: resync REFETCHES current truth from source; a resync that reuses in-memory stale state => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING (scenario-first #126; expert fix pre-built 8d04af8a2 to design 0b9aa6dc7, marker pending): seed a resync that trusts in-memory state (no refetch) while source has changed => stale/RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: If reconnect OR resync FAILS, the client FAILS LOUD (a visible stale/disconnected indicator), NEVER silent-stale. A dead-but-silent transport is the exact defect (the DOM looks live but is frozen).

gateRef.assertion: reconnect/resync failure => visible fail-loud state, never a silently-frozen live-looking DOM

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING (scenario-first #126; expert fix pre-built 8d04af8a2 to design 0b9aa6dc7, marker pending): seed a reconnect that cannot succeed -> visible fail-loud; a silent-frozen DOM on failure => RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: NO UA-sniff / iOS-detection / platform branch — the fix is GENERAL-CORRECT via the standard lifecycle events (visibilitychange/pageshow), so it works on every browser that suspends, not just today's iOS Safari. A UA/platform branch in the transport-lifecycle path => RED.

gateRef.assertion: transport-lifecycle uses standard lifecycle events only; a UA-sniff/iOS-detection branch => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING (scenario-first #126; expert fix pre-built 8d04af8a2 to design 0b9aa6dc7, marker pending): seed a UA-sniff/navigator.platform branch gating the resync => RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: TESTER SEVERED-CHANNEL GATE (stub-must-fail): programmatically SEVER the socket, mutate the data at source, then foreground/visibility-restore -> the view RESYNCS to current (not stale). A build where the severed-then-foregrounded view stays stale => RED. Proves the resync actually catches a dead channel.

gateRef.assertion: sever socket -> change data -> foreground -> view resyncs to current; stays-stale => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING (scenario-first #126; expert fix pre-built 8d04af8a2 to design 0b9aa6dc7, marker pending): the gate's own stub (severed + stale-after-foreground) observed RED before the fix counts as proven

Headless/desktop-WebKit CANNOT mock the iOS transport-suspend, so DESKTOP-GREEN IS NOT FIXED. Only Tron's real-device confirm closes this (asserts the RENDERED live state on his actual device, not a proxy).

gateRef.assertion: real iOS: bg/lock -> change -> foreground -> view live-current, no reload; desktop-green does NOT satisfy
